title: The Explicit Base-p Carry Recurrence Behind Kummer's Theorem
description: The parent entry (oq-01-oq-01) restates Kummer's theorem with a named carryCount — the count of carries when k and n−k are added in base p — computed through the global modular condition pⁱ ≤ (a mod pⁱ) + (b mod pⁱ). That count is correct but non-local: it never exhibits a carry as something propagated digit-by-digit. This follow-up supplies the missing local layer. It defines the single carry bit cᵢ = ⌊(m mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ)/pⁱ⌋ ∈ {0,1} and proves the schoolbook recurrence c₀ = 0, c_{i+1} = ⌊(dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) + cᵢ)/p⌋, where dᵢ(x) = ⌊x/pⁱ⌋ mod p — the carry is literally ⌊(column sum + incoming carry)/p⌋. Neither Mathlib nor the parent proves this recurrence. From it the entry recovers vₚ(C(m+n, m)) as a sum of carry bits and, crucially, sharpens the parent's carryCount = 0 corollary to the genuinely digitwise no-carry criterion: p ∤ C(m+n, m) iff dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) < p for every i. This is open question oq-01 of the parent Kummer carry-count entry.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 (Mathlib)
meta.assumptions: None beyond Lean's foundational propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound. The file contains no axiom declarations, no sorry, and no native_decide (the only decide calls are on small concrete numerals, so they reduce in the kernel and introduce no Lean.ofReduceBool). The single deep mathematical input is Mathlib's Kummer theorem padicValNat_choose', which states vₚ(C(n+k, k)) equals the cardinality of {i ∈ Ico 1 b | pⁱ ≤ k mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ}; the file adds the explicit carry recurrence and the digitwise no-carry criterion on top of it. The carry bit, the digit decomposition x mod p^{i+1} = x mod pⁱ + pⁱ·dᵢ(x) (Nat.mod_mul), the recurrence c_{i+1} = ⌊(dᵢm + dᵢn + cᵢ)/p⌋ (Nat.mul_add_div and Nat.div_div_eq_div_mul), the bit bound cᵢ ≤ 1, the bridge carry = indicator of pⁱ ≤ … , and the no-carry equivalence are all proved in-file by elementary natural-number arithmetic and induction. The three worked instances (carry 10 7 5 1 = 1, carry 10 7 5 0 = 0, digit 10 753 1 = 5) close by decide on small concrete numerals (kernel reduction, not native_decide).

overview.historicalContext: Ernst Kummer (1852) showed that the exact power of a prime p dividing C(m+n, m) is the number of carries when m and n are added in base p. The carry count is usually described algorithmically — add the base-p digits column by column, carrying a 1 whenever a column sum reaches p — yet most formal developments, Mathlib and the parent gallery entry included, state the theorem through the equivalent but non-local condition pⁱ ≤ (m mod pⁱ) + (n mod pⁱ). That global inequality counts carries correctly but hides their recursive nature: it never says a carry out of column i depends on the carry into column i. This follow-up restores the schoolbook recurrence c_{i+1} = ⌊(dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) + cᵢ)/p⌋, connects it back to the modular form (and thence to Mathlib's valuation), and reads off the sharper digitwise criterion that p ∤ C(m+n, m) exactly when no column dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) ever reaches p.
overview.problemStatement: Refine the parent entry's modular carryCount by exhibiting the local carry. Define the carry bit cᵢ into position i for the addition of m and n, prove it is genuinely a single bit obeying c₀ = 0 and the schoolbook recurrence c_{i+1} = ⌊(dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) + cᵢ)/p⌋, where dᵢ(x) = ⌊x/pⁱ⌋ mod p. Show the carry bit equals the indicator of the modular carry condition, hence vₚ(C(m+n, m)) = Σᵢ cᵢ. Sharpen the parent's carryCount = 0 corollary to the digitwise criterion: p ∤ C(m+n, m) iff dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) < p for all i.
overview.text: The carries of Kummer's theorem are generated by the schoolbook recurrence c_{i+1} = ⌊(dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) + cᵢ)/p⌋; consequently p ∤ C(m+n, m) iff no base-p column dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) reaches p.
overview.proofStrategy: The carry into position i is defined globally as carry p m n i = ⌊(m mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ)/pⁱ⌋, matching the parent's and Mathlib's notion. Three facts make it usable. (1) carry_le_one: each mod is below pⁱ, so the sum is below 2·pⁱ and the quotient is ≤ 1 (Nat.div_lt_of_lt_mul). (2) mod_pow_succ_eq: peeling a digit, x mod p^{i+1} = x mod pⁱ + pⁱ·dᵢ(x), is exactly Nat.mod_mul after pow_succ. (3) carry_succ, the recurrence: substituting the digit decomposition into carry at i+1 gives a numerator pⁱ·(dᵢm + dᵢn) + (m mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ); dividing by p^{i+1} = pⁱ·p via Nat.div_div_eq_div_mul and Nat.mul_add_div collapses it to ⌊(dᵢm + dᵢn + cᵢ)/p⌋, the incoming carry surfacing as ⌊(m mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ)/pⁱ⌋. The bridge carry_eq_indicator turns carry into the Boolean of pⁱ ≤ (m mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ) using Nat.one_le_div_iff with the bit bound. Summing the indicators over Ico 1 b and invoking Mathlib's padicValNat_choose' yields padicValNat_choose_eq_sum_carry. For the sharper corollary, forall_carry_zero_iff runs the recurrence both ways (a carry of 0 forces the column below p; all columns below p keep every carry at 0 by induction); carries past the leading digit vanish (carry_eq_zero_of_lt) so the finite condition lifts to all i, and ¬ p ∣ C(m+n, m) ⇔ padicValNat = 0 ⇔ every carry is 0 ⇔ every column is below p.
keyInsights: **The carry is a recurrence, not just a modular inequality.** The parent entry and Mathlib state Kummer through pⁱ ≤ (m mod pⁱ) + (n mod pⁱ) — correct but non-local. The content of carry_succ is that this global condition is generated by the one-line schoolbook rule c_{i+1} = ⌊(dᵢm + dᵢn + cᵢ)/p⌋; the carry literally is ⌊(column sum + incoming carry)/p⌋. This recurrence is in neither Mathlib nor the parent.

**One algebraic identity drives the recurrence.** Writing m mod p^{i+1} = m mod pⁱ + pⁱ·dᵢ(m) (Nat.mod_mul) turns the numerator at level i+1 into pⁱ·(dᵢm + dᵢn) + (m mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ). Because the trailing remainder is below pⁱ, dividing by pⁱ·p factors cleanly as ⌊(dᵢm + dᵢn + ⌊remainder/pⁱ⌋)/p⌋ — and ⌊remainder/pⁱ⌋ is exactly the previous carry.

**A carry is a single bit.** Since m mod pⁱ and n mod pⁱ are each below pⁱ, their sum is below 2·pⁱ, so the quotient by pⁱ is 0 or 1. This bit bound is what lets the carry double as the indicator of pⁱ ≤ (m mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ) and makes the sum of carries a literal count matching the parent's carryCount.

**Sharpening carryCount = 0 to a digitwise criterion.** The parent's not-divisible corollary stops at carryCount = 0 (the modular count vanishes). Running the recurrence both ways upgrades this to the genuinely local statement p ∤ C(m+n, m) ⇔ dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) < p for all i: a single column reaching p is what forces a carry, hence a factor of p. At p = 2 this is the classic 'C(m+n, m) is odd iff m and n have disjoint binary supports'.

**Delegating the valuation, owning the structure.** The actual computation that vₚ(C(m+n, m)) counts carries is Mathlib's padicValNat_choose' (and the parent's restatement); this follow-up contributes the structural layer both lack — the explicit carry recurrence and the digitwise unit criterion — assembled by elementary arithmetic with no new axioms.
prerequisites: Parent entry (oq-01-oq-01): Kummer's carry-count theorem with the named carryCount and its modular divisibility corollaries
Kummer's theorem in Mathlib: padicValNat_choose' (valuation of a binomial as a count of modular carries)
p-adic valuation API: padicValNat_dvd_iff_le and the Fact p.Prime convention
Base-p digit arithmetic: Nat.mod_mul (x mod (a·b) = x mod a + a·(x/a mod b)), pow_succ

Natural-number division: Nat.mul_add_div, Nat.div_div_eq_div_mul, Nat.div_lt_of_lt_mul, Nat.one_le_div_iff, Nat.div_eq_zero_iff; Finset.card_filter, Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg, Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self

conclusion.summary: The base-p carry into position i for the addition of m and n is defined and shown to be a single bit obeying the schoolbook recurrence c_{i+1} = ⌊(dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) + cᵢ)/p⌋ (carry_succ) — the local structure neither Mathlib nor the parent entry exposes. It equals the indicator of the modular carry condition (carry_eq_indicator), so vₚ(C(m+n, m)) is the sum of carry bits over Ico 1 b (padicValNat_choose_eq_sum_carry), matching the parent's carryCount. Running the recurrence both ways sharpens the parent's carryCount = 0 corollary to the digitwise no-carry criterion: p ∤ C(m+n, m) iff dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) < p for every i (not_dvd_choose_iff_no_carry). All 9 theorems are fully verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms; the only deep input is Mathlib's padicValNat_choose'.
conclusion.implications: The explicit carry recurrence is the missing algorithmic layer over the modular statement of Kummer's theorem: it makes 'carries when adding in base p' a literal recursive computation rather than a count of inequalities, and it yields the unit criterion p ∤ C(m+n, m) ⇔ no column reaches p directly. This is the engine behind classical results such as the count of binomial coefficients in a row of Pascal's triangle not divisible by p (a product over base-p digits) and Lucas' congruence, and it specialises at p = 2 to the statement that C(m+n, m) is odd iff m and n have disjoint binary supports.
openQuestions: Count the entries in row N of Pascal's triangle not divisible by p as ∏ᵢ (dᵢ(N) + 1), deriving it from the digitwise no-carry criterion and Lucas' congruence.
Give the exact valuation vₚ(C(m+n, m)) as a closed digit-sum (Sₚ(m) + Sₚ(n) − Sₚ(m+n))/(p−1), reconciling the carry count with Legendre's digit-sum form from the grandparent entry.

crossReferences.description: Parent entry. It restates Kummer's theorem with the modular carryCount and stops the no-carry corollary at carryCount = 0; this follow-up exhibits the explicit carry recurrence that generates carryCount and sharpens the corollary to the digitwise criterion dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) < p.
Grandparent entry: Legendre's formula for vₚ(n!), whose digit-sum form is the natural target for converting the carry count proved here into a closed digit-sum expression.

sections.title: Overview and Setup
sections.summary: Docstring framing the follow-up against the parent's modular carryCount, motivating the local schoolbook recurrence. Imports the p-adic valuation basics, opens Nat / Finset, and defines digit (the i-th base-p digit) and carry (the carry bit into position i).

sections.title: The Carry Bit and the Digit Decomposition
sections.summary: carry_zero (no carry into the units place), carry_le_one (a carry is 0 or 1, since two remainders below pⁱ sum below 2·pⁱ), and mod_pow_succ_eq (peeling one digit: x mod p^{i+1} = x mod pⁱ + pⁱ·dᵢ(x), via Nat.mod_mul).

sections.title: The Schoolbook Carry Recurrence
sections.summary: carry_succ: c_{i+1} = ⌊(dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) + cᵢ)/p⌋, the digit-by-digit carry rule, proved by substituting the digit decomposition and collapsing the division of pⁱ·(dᵢm+dᵢn) + remainder by pⁱ·p. carry_eq_zero_of_lt records that carries vanish past the leading digit (m + n < pⁱ ⟹ cᵢ = 0).

sections.title: Bridge to Mathlib and the Carry-Bit Sum
sections.summary: carry_eq_indicator identifies the carry bit with the Boolean of pⁱ ≤ (m mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ). Summing the indicators and invoking padicValNat_choose' gives padicValNat_choose_eq_sum_carry: vₚ(C(m+n, m)) = Σ over Ico 1 b of carry bits, the recurrence-based form of the parent's carryCount identity.

sections.title: The Digitwise No-Carry Criterion and Instances
sections.summary: forall_carry_zero_iff runs the recurrence both ways to equate 'all carries 0' with 'every column dᵢ(m)+dᵢ(n) < p'. not_dvd_choose_iff_no_carry lifts the finite condition to all i (carries vanish past the leading digit) and concludes p ∤ C(m+n, m) ⇔ dᵢ(m)+dᵢ(n) < p for all i, sharpening the parent's carryCount = 0 form. Three decide-checked instances illustrate carry and digit.
